slides.title: A Different Type of Story
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 5 English, Unit 6: A Different Type of Story. This unit explores the different types of story writers create. You will meet five genres on the library shelves — adventure, mystery, fable, legend and realistic fiction — and learn the features that tell them apart. A courtroom story then shows realistic fiction at work, while twenty-five words built from the prefixes un-, dis- and in- and the endings -ible, -able and -ous stretch your vocabulary. Alongside this you will learn to link ideas smoothly with conjunctions and connective adverbs, and use them to write your own story opening. In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.title: What you will achieve
bullets: Identify and compare the five story genres in this unit and describe the features of each.
Support inferences about characters, viewpoint and language choices with evidence from the text.
Work out the meaning of longer words from the prefixes un-, dis-, in- and the endings -ible, -able and -ous.
slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to identify and compare the five story genres in this unit and describe the features of each. You will also support inferences about characters, viewpoint and language choices with evidence from the text. You will also work out the meaning of longer words from the prefixes un-, dis-, in- and the endings -ible, -able and -ous. Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Language for precise thinking
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: unrest, uneasy, unexpected, unsuccessful, unfamiliar, uncertain. Listen to each pronunciation in the vocabulary lab, study its meaning in context, and use the word accurately in your own discussion and writing.

slides.title: Read critically
bullets: The Library Tour: Adventure and Mystery
The Library Tour: Fable, Legend and Realistic Fiction
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes The Library Tour: Adventure and Mystery and The Library Tour: Fable, Legend and Realistic Fiction. Read actively. Identify each text's central ideas, notice viewpoint and reliability, and support every inference with relevant evidence from the text.

slides.title: What Are Connectives and Conjunctions?
bullets: A connective is any word or phrase that links ideas across your writing. A conjunction is one kind of connective, and it joins words, phrases or clauses...
slides.narration: The first language focus is What Are Connectives and Conjunctions? A connective is any word or phrase that links ideas across your writing. A conjunction is one kind of connective, and it joins words, phrases or clauses inside a single sentence. Notice the structure in the model examples, then apply it deliberately in connected sentences and paragraphs.

slides.title: Use English for a real purpose
bullets: Writing 1: Plan and Write a Story Opening
Explain, support and improve your ideas
slides.narration: In speaking, you will complete Speaking 1: Genre Detective Game. Organise your ideas, use evidence and respond clearly to questions. In writing, you will plan, draft, check and revise. Use the success criteria before submitting your work.

slides.title: You are ready to begin
bullets: Activities, quiz and optional live sessions
slides.narration: You are ready to begin. Start with the vocabulary lab, continue through reading and comprehension, apply the grammar focus, and complete the speaking and writing practices. Use the AI tutor for hints and feedback any time, and bring your questions to a live session too if you join one.
